newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian confectioner '95 net profit 14.8 mln kuna.
newsitem.headline: Croatian confectioner '95 net profit 14.8 mln kuna.

text.p: Croatian confectioner Kras d.d. posted a consolidated net profit of 14.8 million kuna for the year ended December 31, 1995, down from 15.3 million a year earlier.

Profit for the parent company, which has been in talks with the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) about possible investment, shrank to 14.56 million kuna from just over 15 million in 1994.

The chocolate maker reported consolidated pre-tax profit shrinking to 15.0 million kuna from 17.3 million as its costs climbed 27.6 million kuna to 639.3 million, overshooting a handsome income rise to over 654 million.
But Kras said in the annual report it had "maintained and reinforced a leading position on the domestic market".

"Production increased 3.0 percent, total sales 2.9 percent, domestic sales 9.5 percent," president of the board Boris Marcac said in a letter to shareholders, adding that Kras's market share was 38.6 percent in 1995.
Marcac said a six kuna dividend for 1995 would be proposed to the annual shareholders' meeting on September 28, following 5.65 kuna per share on 1994 results.
The company has adopted a restructuring plan under which it will switch to two instead of three working shifts to cut down costs.
Kras also plans to invest a considerable portion of its 1995 proceeds into further development and modernisation of the existing production capacities.
Its shares, listed on the semi-regulated segment of the Zagreb Stock Exchange, have been rising steadily in the past weeks, fetching 315 kuna last Friday.
